A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same grounding study and RIFTS benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, Tables 1–9, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dialogue-log analyses, human annotation validation, grounding-forecasting experiments, and RIFTS evaluations of models and the GROUND intervention.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical analyses and experimental outcomes, including the main-text and appendix results.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o-mini annotator, Llama-3.1-8B forecasting procedure, weighted training loss, and selective GROUND intervention remain unchanged. Section 5.2 adds explanatory examples; renaming Ambiguous acts to Disambiguating does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English-language WildChat, Bing Chat, and MultiWOZ 2.2 coverage and the same 1,740-task RIFTS benchmark. No additional evaluated task, domain, population, or scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 6 retains the few-shot GPT-4o-mini forecasting baseline. Tables 3 and 7 retain the same GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, o3-mini, Claude Sonnet 3.5, Claude Opus 3, and Llama 3.1 comparison models.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes the accuracy rule's 'neither' branch from No Action tasks to tasks outside Addressing and Disambiguating. This also includes Advancing tasks, creating overlap with the follow-up branch. This is a change to the stated metric; the PDFs do not establish changed scoring implementation or rerun experiments.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 adds a brief qualitative diagnosis of annotation disagreements, identifying confusion between clarification and follow-up questions. The compounding-failure and lexical analyses remain unchanged. The new forecasting examples are explicitly hypothetical, rather than additional experimental case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same 95% confidence-interval reporting in Table 3, t-test reporting in Section 5.1, and lexical z-scores in Appendix A.2. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The numerical results remain unchanged, including forecasting macro AUROC of 0.51 versus 0.61 in Table 6 and GROUND accuracy of 54.48 in Table 3. Section 5.1 newly reports the qualitative finding that much early annotation disagreement concerned clarification versus follow-up.

T1.justification: The piecewise accuracy definition in Section 6 is mathematically revised: its final condition now overlaps the Advancing condition, whereas v1 restricted it to No Action. The forecasting equations and Appendix B loss remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract softens the intervention claim from an intervention 'that mitigates' grounding failures to one 'aimed at mitigating' them. This is a limited qualification: the introduction still calls the intervention effective, and the main study and benchmark contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of forecasting as marginalizing over assistant responses, explicitly motivates RIFTS through prompts requiring grounding regardless of the response, and discusses pretraining biases and theory-of-mind limitations as possible explanations for model behavior. The existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly documents discussion and reannotation before reaching the reported agreement of 0.71. This provides additional validation-process detail without establishing a newly conducted study. Appendix hyperparameters, hardware, filtering instructions, and resource-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Grice (1975), Hewitt et al. (2024), Sap et al. (2022), and Ullman (2023). These support the discussion of overresponses, instruction-following biases, and theory-of-mind limitations; the broader related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 renames Ambiguous acts to Disambiguating, makes scattered language corrections, expands the forecasting and benchmark-curation explanations, and adds a discussion paragraph. The section hierarchy and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 change their axis label from Percentage to Proportion while retaining the plotted values. Table labels and captions are revised, Table 1 gains explanatory annotations, and Section 5.2 gains illustrated examples. Tables 2 and 3 move with text reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves forecasting explanations and annotation transparency, but introduces overlapping conditions in the central RIFTS scoring definition, which was unambiguous in v1. The numerical results remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether the revised condition was used in scoring. These explanatory benefits and the new methodological ambiguity leave the net quality direction uncertain.
